item.description: Every block today circles back to the same two forces: the Bank of Canada holding rates, and oil spiking because of the fighting between the United States and Iran. That overlap is the real story. The Bank held its overnight rate at 2.25 percent Wednesday, the seventh straight hold, after second quarter growth came in at 3.3 percent and unemployment eased to 6.4 percent. 2026-09-03 Markets & Economy: Markets & Economy
item.description: - The Bank of Canada held at 2.25 percent and is watching both Middle East oil prices and the trade war before its next move on October 28. - Ottawa's countertariffs on 27.6 billion dollars of US goods take effect September 8, so expect price pressure in categories like steel, appliances, and some food items this fall. - Toronto home sales cooled in August after five months of gains, with prices down but inventory tightening, which could support prices later this year. - Oil above 90 dollars and Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions are the wildcard behind both inflation risk and the TSX's energy led strength this week. - Fixed mortgage rates are still drifting higher even with the Bank on hold, so renewal timing conversations matter more than usual right now.

item.title: 2026-09-03 The Ten: Nvidia, Google, and Broadcom Lead Global Business Talk
item.description: - Bank of Canada held at 2.25% for a seventh straight time, but two big banks now call for hikes by December. - Nvidia just spent almost 13 billion dollars on Hugging Face, its second biggest deal ever. - A federal judge let Google keep its ad exchange, the third Big Tech breakup bid to fail in a row. - Air Canada is adding routes overseas while its regional flight attendants vote on a strike mandate. - BRP posted a quarterly loss but still raised its full year guidance despite US tariffs.

item.title: 2026-09-03 Practice: Tax, Regulatory & Industry: Practice: Tax, Regulatory & Industry
item.description: - The Bank of Canada held at 2.25 percent again but the tone was more hawkish on inflation than growth, so don't assume the next move is automatically a cut. - If you're incorporated and sitting on a large investment portfolio inside the company, this year's passive income determines next year's tax rate on active income, so let's review the AAII number now. - The 2026 numbers are locked in: 7,000 dollars of new TFSA room, 33,810 dollars of RRSP room, 8,000 dollars into an FHSA if you're a first-time buyer. - Manitoba's grocery sales tax exemption already kicked in July 1, but the bigger affordability credit changes, including a clawback for homes over a million dollars, don't start until the 2027 tax year. - If you're planning to hand down a cottage or a business, get the lawyer, the accountant, and the insurance review happening together this fall, not after the fact.

item.title: 2026-09-03 Manitoba & Winnipeg: Hydro Turbines, Rate Hold, and a Mayor's Race Heats Up
item.description: - The Brandon turbine deal with GE Vernova is not finalized, and the premier is publicly hedging on whether Manitoba proceeds with a U.S. supplier. - The Bank of Canada held at 2.25 percent for a seventh straight time, with the next decision not until October 28th. - Winnipeg's mayoral race just turned personal, with Kevin Klein's Nygard ties already being used against him by both a cabinet minister and the incumbent mayor. - StandardAero just opened a 70,000 square foot expansion in Winnipeg, a genuine good-news jobs story in the aerospace sector. - A Dynacare lab strike and a provincial essential-services request collide next week, which could disrupt routine blood work and diagnostic testing across Manitoba.

item.title: 2026-09-03 Climate Policy & Nonprofit Governance: Trade War, Rate Hold, and Charity Sector Shifts
item.description: - Manitoba Hydro rates are going up 3.5 percent a year through 2028, so budget conversations with Manitoba clients should build that in now. - Efficiency Manitoba still has active heat pump and insulation rebates, worth raising with any client doing a renovation this fall. - The Bank of Canada held at 2.25 percent, but National Bank and Scotiabank are now calling for hikes by December, which is a real split from the other big banks. - If you sit on a charity board, confirm your organization is registered for CRA's online services, since the fax line and advance purpose approvals are both gone. - United Way Winnipeg posted a record 23.3 million dollar campaign last year, a genuine bright spot against a national trend of declining charitable donations.

item.title: 2026-09-03 AI & Technology: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face, OpenAI's Astra Rattles Safety Camp
item.description: - Nvidia's 12.9 billion dollar purchase of Hugging Face shows the AI infrastructure fight has moved to who controls the open model ecosystem, not just chips. - OpenAI's new Astra model uses a reasoning technique that safety researchers say makes it harder to monitor what the model is actually thinking before it acts. - Washington wants light-touch AI rules globally while the UK Parliament is drafting kill switch powers, so multinational AI exposure means navigating two very different regulatory paths at once. - Canada's new data centre framework, signed by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft, sets ground rules on power costs and water use right as public opposition to local buildouts grows. - The Bank of Canada held rates at 2.25 percent for a seventh straight decision, but two major banks are now calling for a hike by December instead of a cut.

item.title: 2026-09-03 Health & Fitness: Immune Aging Breakthrough, Muscle Science, and Fall Health Watch
item.description: - A Stanford study in mice found blocking one immune receptor kept multiple organs measurably younger, but it's animal research, not a treatment yet. - People who do any muscle-strengthening activity have roughly 10 to 17 percent lower all-cause mortality, and pairing it with cardio pushes that benefit higher. - About one hour of resistance training a week appears to capture most of the longevity benefit, so consistency beats marathon gym sessions. - Aim for 30 to 40 grams of protein per meal rather than obsessing over pre-sleep timing, the daily total matters more than the clock. - The Bank of Canada held rates at 2.25 percent for a seventh straight decision, with two big banks now betting on a hike by December.

item.title: 2026-09-03 Parenting: Money Stress, Benefits, and Child Care Updates Today
item.description: - The Canada Child Benefit rose again this July, worth confirming your clients' new monthly amount. - EI parental leave maximums went up in 2026, so the standard versus extended choice is worth re-running the numbers on. - Manitoba's $10-a-day child care is real, but space availability is lagging well behind the province's own target. - RESP contributions timed early in a child's life still capture the fullest government matching. - The Bank of Canada held rates again this week, its seventh straight hold, with a split outlook heading into October.

item.title: 2026-09-03 Sports: Jets Trade Winds, Bombers Ready For Regina
item.description: - The Jets goalie situation is a story, not a rumor. Hellebuyck confirmed the trade request himself, and Winnipeg is under no cap pressure to move fast given his contract runs through 2031. - The Bombers are 6 and 5 heading into Sunday's Labour Day Classic in Regina against a 7 and 4 Saskatchewan team, with the Banjo Bowl rematch back home the following Saturday. - Kawhi Leonard is officially clear to join the Raptors after the NBA fined him 700 thousand dollars personally but hammered the Clippers with 30 million in fines and five stripped first round picks. - Patrick Mahomes says he feels on track to start Week 1 against Denver on Monday Night Football, September 14, less than nine months after ACL and LCL surgery. - There is a genuine wealth planning angle in hockey right now, with a Tax Court of Canada case involving Tavares and Marleau testing how the CRA treats signing bonuses under the Canada U.S. tax treaty.
